title: The best startup mentor is a flight instructor
structureWhy: Clip-first, per the yc-sam-01 data (32% hold opening on b-roll + narration, vs ~63% for clip-only cuts opening on a face). clip:0 and clip:1 are consecutive so no transition fires between them.

source.speaker: Sam Altman
source.comment: FULL-FRAME 3840x2160, not pre-cropped. The opening passage is a wide two-shot that must keep its composition, so the crop has to be decided per passage rather than baked into the file.
source.passagesWhy: 0: opens cold on the relatable problem - energy and ambition with nowhere to point it. 1: the whole teacher / lecture / flight-instructor analogy, uncut, because the contrast IS the idea. The wide two-shot that preceded this was cut: it set up who Paul Graham is, but the badge does that job at the moment his name is spoken, and the interviewer compliment cost 2s without earning them.
source.subjectFocusWhy: Head sits at ~0.35 of the source frame and he faces screen-right, so the window shifts right to leave looking room in the direction he's facing.

publish.title: The Best Startup Mentor Is a Flight Instructor
publish.description:
Sam Altman on Paul Graham's idea that a good investor is a teacher — but not the kind who gives lectures.

Commentary and edit: The Next Curve

rights.speaker: Sam Altman
rights.note: Short excerpts as evidence for original commentary. Narration is the spine.

captionCorrectionsWhy: ASR heard 'teacher as someone' as 'teachers, someone'. Clip captions have no script to check against, so mishearings ship as on-screen typos.

beats.why: lands on 'Paul had this thing he used to say' - identify him at the moment he is named, not before
beats.caption: PAUL GRAHAM

beats.why: 'someone who gives a lecture' — show the lecture hall
'a lecture about a startup' — empty seats, the idea failing to land
'like a flight instructor' — the image the whole analogy turns on
'do this, don't do this' — corrective, hands-on instruction
